AFG.name: Afghanistan
AFG.geographicScope: Afghanistan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
AFG.relationship: Southern Asia, north and west of Pakistan, east of Iran. Independent country.
AFG.languages: Dari (Afghan Persian) and Pashto; Uzbeki, Turkmani and other languages are also spoken.

population.note: Archived estimate; conflict and displacement create substantial uncertainty.

AFG.highlight: The Hindu Kush mountains run northeast to southwest, separating northern Afghanistan from much of the rest of the country.

ALD.name: Åland
ALD.geographicScope: The autonomous Åland archipelago, separately mapped from the rest of Finland; population is Åland only.
ALD.relationship: Autonomous region of Finland in the Baltic Sea, between Finland and Sweden.
ALD.languages: Swedish (official); Finnish and other languages are also spoken.

population.note: Year-end population rose from 30,654 in 2024 to 30,836 in 2025 (Statistics Åland).

ALD.highlight: Åland is demilitarised and has its own parliament; its maritime traditions are preserved in the Åland Maritime Museum.

ALB.name: Albania
ALB.geographicScope: Albania profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ALB.relationship: Southeastern Europe, bordering the Adriatic Sea and Ionian Sea, between Greece to the south and Montenegro and Kosovo to the north. Independent country.
ALB.languages: Albanian; Greek and other minority languages.
ALB.highlight: Strategic location along Strait of Otranto (links Adriatic Sea to Ionian Sea and Mediterranean Sea).

DZA.name: Algeria
DZA.geographicScope: Algeria profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
DZA.relationship: Northern Africa, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, between Morocco and Tunisia. Independent country.
DZA.languages: Arabic and Tamazight; French is also widely used.
DZA.highlight: Terrain: mostly high plateau and desert; Atlas Mountains in the far north and Hoggar Mountains in the south; narrow, discontinuous coastal plain; highest point: Tahat 2,908 m.

ASM.name: American Samoa
ASM.geographicScope: American Samoa profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ASM.relationship: Oceania, group of islands in the South Pacific Ocean, about halfway between Hawaii and New Zealand. Unincorporated, unorganized Territory of the US.
ASM.languages: Samoan and English; Tongan and other Pacific languages.
ASM.highlight: Pago Pago has one of the best natural deepwater harbors in the South Pacific Ocean, sheltered by shape from rough seas and protected by peripheral mountains from high winds; strategic location in the South Pacific Ocean.

AND.name: Andorra
AND.geographicScope: Andorra profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
AND.relationship: Southwestern Europe, Pyrenees mountains, on the border between France and Spain. Independent country.
AND.highlight: Landlocked; straddles a number of important crossroads in the Pyrenees.

AGO.name: Angola
AGO.geographicScope: Angola profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
AGO.relationship: Southern Africa, bordering the South Atlantic Ocean, between Namibia and Democratic Republic of the Congo. Independent country.
AGO.languages: Portuguese, Umbundu, Kikongo, Kimbundu, Chokwe and other languages.
AGO.highlight: The province of Cabinda is an exclave, separated from the rest of the country by the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

AIA.name: Anguilla
AIA.geographicScope: Anguilla profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
AIA.relationship: Caribbean, islands between the Caribbean Sea and North Atlantic Ocean, east of Puerto Rico. Overseas territory of the UK.
AIA.highlight: The most northerly of the Leeward Islands in the Lesser Antilles.

ATG.name: Antigua and Barbuda
ATG.geographicScope: Antigua and Barbuda profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ATG.relationship: Caribbean, islands between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, east-southeast of Puerto Rico. Independent country.
ATG.highlight: Antigua has a deeply indented shoreline with many natural harbors and beaches; Barbuda has a large western harbor.

ARG.name: Argentina
ARG.geographicScope: Argentina profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ARG.relationship: Southern South America, bordering the South Atlantic Ocean, between Chile and Uruguay. Independent country.
ARG.languages: Spanish; Italian and Indigenous languages including Quechua, Guarani and Mapudungun.
ARG.highlight: Second-largest country in South America (after Brazil).

ARM.name: Armenia
ARM.geographicScope: Armenia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ARM.relationship: Southwestern Asia, between Turkey (to the west) and Azerbaijan; note - Armenia views itself as part of Europe; geopolitically, it can be classified as falling within Europe, the Middle East, or both. Independent country.
ARM.languages: Armenian; Russian and Ezidian are also spoken.
ARM.highlight: Landlocked in the Lesser Caucasus Mountains; Sevana Lich (Lake Sevan) is the largest lake in this mountain range.

ABW.name: Aruba
ABW.geographicScope: Aruba profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ABW.relationship: Caribbean, island in the Caribbean Sea, north of Venezuela. One of four constituent countries of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
ABW.languages: Papiamento and Dutch; Spanish and English are also spoken.
ABW.highlight: A flat, riverless island known for its white sand beaches; its tropical climate is moderated by constant trade winds from the Atlantic Ocean; the temperature is almost constant at about 27 degrees Celsius (81 degrees Fahrenheit).

ATC.name: Ashmore and Cartier Islands
ATC.geographicScope: Ashmore and Cartier Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ATC.relationship: Australian external territory in the Indian Ocean, between northwestern Australia and Timor.

population.period: No dated resident-population series in the archived source.
population.note: The archived source reports no permanent inhabitants; temporary personnel are not a resident population.

ATC.highlight: Ashmore Reef National Nature Reserve established in 1983; Cartier Island Marine Reserve established in 2000.

AUS.name: Australia
AUS.geographicScope: Australian national profile; the map includes the mainland, Tasmania and other islands. Separately mapped Australian external territories have their own cards.
AUS.relationship: Independent country spanning the Australian mainland, Tasmania and other islands between the Indian and Pacific oceans.
AUS.languages: English; Mandarin, Arabic, Vietnamese, Cantonese and many other languages.
AUS.highlight: World's smallest continent but sixth-largest country; the largest country in Oceania, the largest country entirely in the Southern Hemisphere, and the largest country without land borders.

IOA.name: Australian Indian Ocean Territories
IOA.geographicScope: Natural Earth groups Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands into this map entity; Australia’s mainland population is not used.
IOA.relationship: Two Australian external territories in the Indian Ocean, south and southwest of Indonesia: Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands.
IOA.languages: English, Mandarin and other Chinese languages on Christmas Island; Cocos Malay and English on the Cocos (Keeling) Islands.

population.period: No comparable combined trend is published for the two territories.
population.note: Sum of archived 2021 estimates: Christmas Island 1,692 plus Cocos (Keeling) Islands 593. Christmas Island’s older growth rate is not applied to the group.

IOA.highlight: The Cocos group consists of coral islands around a lagoon, while Christmas Island lies farther east along Indian Ocean sea routes.

AUT.name: Austria
AUT.geographicScope: Austria profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
AUT.relationship: Central Europe, north of Italy and Slovenia. Independent country.
AUT.languages: German; Turkish, Serbian, Croatian, Slovene and Hungarian are also spoken.
AUT.highlight: Terrain: mostly mountains (Alps) in the west and south; mostly flat or gently sloping along the eastern and northern margins; highest point: Grossglockner 3,798 m.

AZE.name: Azerbaijan
AZE.geographicScope: Azerbaijan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
AZE.relationship: Southwestern Asia, bordering the Caspian Sea, between Iran and Russia, with a small European portion north of the Caucasus range. Independent country.
AZE.languages: Azerbaijani; Russian, Avar, Talyshi and other minority languages.
AZE.highlight: Both the main area of the country and the Naxcivan exclave are landlocked.

BHR.name: Bahrain
BHR.geographicScope: Bahrain profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BHR.relationship: Middle East, archipelago in the Persian Gulf, east of Saudi Arabia. Independent country.
BHR.highlight: Bahrain’s low desert plain rises to a central escarpment; Jabal ad Dukhan reaches 135 metres.

BGD.name: Bangladesh
BGD.geographicScope: Bangladesh profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BGD.relationship: Southern Asia, bordering the Bay of Bengal, between Burma and India. Independent country.
BGD.languages: Bangla (Bengali); minority languages are also spoken.
BGD.highlight: Most of the country is situated on deltas of large rivers flowing from the Himalayas: the Ganges unites with the Jamuna (main channel of the Brahmaputra) and later joins the Meghna to eventually empty into the Bay of Bengal.

BRB.name: Barbados
BRB.geographicScope: Barbados profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BRB.relationship: Caribbean, island in the North Atlantic Ocean, northeast of Venezuela. Independent country.
BRB.languages: English and Bajan, an English-based creole.
BRB.highlight: Terrain: relatively flat; rises gently to central highland region; highest point: Mount Hillaby 336 m.

BLR.name: Belarus
BLR.geographicScope: Belarus profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BLR.relationship: Eastern Europe, east of Poland. Independent country.
BLR.languages: Belarusian and Russian; Polish and Ukrainian minorities.
BLR.highlight: Landlocked; glacial scouring accounts for the flatness of Belarusian terrain and for its 11,000 lakes.

BEL.name: Belgium
BEL.geographicScope: Belgium profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BEL.relationship: Western Europe, bordering the North Sea, between France and the Netherlands. Independent country.
BEL.highlight: The landscape changes from flat northwestern coastal plains to the rugged Ardennes in the southeast.

BLZ.name: Belize
BLZ.geographicScope: Belize profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BLZ.relationship: Central America, bordering the Caribbean Sea, between Guatemala and Mexico. Independent country.
BLZ.languages: English, Spanish, Belizean Creole, Maya languages and Garifuna.
BLZ.highlight: Only country in Central America without a coastline on the North Pacific Ocean.

BEN.name: Benin
BEN.geographicScope: Benin profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BEN.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the Bight of Benin, between Nigeria and Togo. Independent country.
BEN.languages: French, Fon, Yoruba, Yom, Bariba, Fulfulde and other languages.
BEN.highlight: Much of Benin is flat or gently rolling; sandbanks restrict access to its Atlantic coast.

BMU.name: Bermuda
BMU.geographicScope: Bermuda profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BMU.relationship: North America, group of islands in the North Atlantic Ocean, east of South Carolina (US). Overseas territory of the UK.
BMU.highlight: Bermuda has many coral islands and cays but no rivers or freshwater lakes.

BTN.name: Bhutan
BTN.geographicScope: Bhutan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BTN.relationship: Southern Asia, between China and India. Independent country.
BTN.languages: Dzongkha, Sharchopkha and Lhotshamkha, among other languages.
BTN.highlight: Landlocked; strategic location between China and India; controls several key Himalayan mountain passes.

BOL.name: Bolivia
BOL.geographicScope: Bolivia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BOL.relationship: Central South America, southwest of Brazil. Independent country.
BOL.languages: Spanish, Quechua, Aymara, Guarani and other Indigenous languages.
BOL.highlight: Lake Titicaca is a high-altitude lake shared with Peru in the Andes.

BIH.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
BIH.geographicScope: Bosnia and Herzegovina profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BIH.relationship: Southeastern Europe, bordering the Adriatic Sea and Croatia. Independent country.
BIH.highlight: Mountains and valleys dominate the landscape; Maglić reaches 2,386 metres.

BWA.name: Botswana
BWA.geographicScope: Botswana profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BWA.relationship: Southern Africa, north of South Africa. Independent country.
BWA.languages: Setswana, Kalanga, Kgalagadi and English, among other languages.
BWA.highlight: Terrain: predominantly flat to gently rolling tableland; Kalahari Desert in southwest; highest point: Manyelanong Hill 1,495 m.

BRA.name: Brazil
BRA.geographicScope: Brazil profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BRA.relationship: Eastern South America, bordering the Atlantic Ocean. Independent country.
BRA.languages: Portuguese; Indigenous languages and immigrant-community languages are also spoken.
BRA.highlight: Largest country in South America and in the Southern Hemisphere.

IOT.name: British Indian Ocean Territory
IOT.geographicScope: Chagos Archipelago under the map’s historical British Indian Ocean Territory label; the cited May 2025 treaty describes a sovereignty settlement but was published before entering into force.
IOT.relationship: Chagos Archipelago in the central Indian Ocean; the map retains its British Indian Ocean Territory label. A UK–Mauritius sovereignty agreement was signed in May 2025.
IOT.languages: No permanent resident language community; the source does not report languages of rotating personnel.

population.period: No dated resident-population series in the archived source.
population.note: Archive reports no permanent inhabitants; Diego Garcia hosts rotating personnel. Chagossians were displaced between 1967 and 1973.

IOT.highlight: Archipelago of 55 islands; Diego Garcia, the largest and southernmost island, occupies a strategic location in the central Indian Ocean.

VGB.name: British Virgin Islands
VGB.geographicScope: British Virgin Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
VGB.relationship: Caribbean, between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, east of Puerto Rico. Overseas territory of the UK.
VGB.highlight: The coral islands are comparatively flat, while the volcanic islands are steep and hilly.

BRN.name: Brunei
BRN.geographicScope: Brunei profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BRN.relationship: Southeastern Asia, along the northern coast of the island of Borneo, bordering the South China Sea and Malaysia. Independent country.
BRN.highlight: Close to vital sea lanes through South China Sea linking Indian and Pacific Oceans; two parts physically separated by Malaysia; the eastern part, the Temburong district, is an exclave and is almost an enclave within Malaysia.

BGR.name: Bulgaria
BGR.geographicScope: Bulgaria profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BGR.relationship: Southeastern Europe, bordering the Black Sea, between Romania and Turkey. Independent country.
BGR.highlight: Mountain ranges contrast with lowlands in the north and southeast; Musala reaches 2,925 metres.

BFA.name: Burkina Faso
BFA.geographicScope: Burkina Faso profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BFA.relationship: Western Africa, north of Ghana. Independent country.
BFA.languages: Mossi, Fula, Gourmantche, Dyula, French and other languages.
BFA.highlight: Landlocked savanna cut by the three principal rivers, the Black, Red, and White Voltas.

BDI.name: Burundi
BDI.geographicScope: Burundi profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BDI.relationship: Central Africa, east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, west of Tanzania. Independent country.
BDI.highlight: Landlocked; straddles crest of the Nile-Congo watershed; the Kagera, which drains into Lake Victoria, is the most remote headstream of the White Nile.

KHM.name: Cambodia
KHM.geographicScope: Cambodia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
KHM.relationship: Southeastern Asia, bordering the Gulf of Thailand, between Thailand, Vietnam, and Laos. Independent country.
KHM.languages: Khmer; minority languages, Chinese and Vietnamese.
KHM.highlight: A land of paddies and forests dominated by the Mekong River and Tonle Sap (Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake).

CMR.name: Cameroon
CMR.geographicScope: Cameroon profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CMR.relationship: Central Africa, bordering the Bight of Biafra, between Equatorial Guinea and Nigeria. Independent country.
CMR.languages: French, English and numerous African languages.
CMR.highlight: Sometimes referred to as the hinge of Africa because of its central location on the continent and its position at the west-south juncture of the Gulf of Guinea.

CAN.name: Canada
CAN.geographicScope: Canada profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CAN.relationship: Northern North America, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean on the east, North Pacific Ocean on the west, and the Arctic Ocean on the north, north of the conterminous US. Independent country.
CAN.languages: English and French; Chinese languages, Punjabi, Spanish, Arabic and many other languages.
CAN.highlight: Canada stretches between the Atlantic, Pacific and Arctic; western mountain ranges contrast with extensive interior plains.

CPV.name: Cape Verde
CPV.geographicScope: Cape Verde profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CPV.relationship: Western Africa, group of islands in the North Atlantic Ocean, west of Senegal. Independent country.
CPV.highlight: Strategic location 500 km from west coast of Africa near major north-south sea routes; one of four North Atlantic archipelagos that make up Macaronesia; the others are Azores (Portugal), Canary Islands (Spain), and Madeira (Portugal).

CYM.name: Cayman Islands
CYM.geographicScope: Cayman Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CYM.relationship: British overseas territory comprising Grand Cayman, Cayman Brac and Little Cayman, south of Cuba in the Caribbean Sea.
CYM.languages: English; Spanish and Filipino are also spoken.
CYM.highlight: The Cayman Islands sit on a low limestone base surrounded by coral reefs.

CAF.name: Central African Republic
CAF.geographicScope: Central African Republic profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CAF.relationship: Central Africa, north of Democratic Republic of the Congo. Independent country.
CAF.languages: French, Sango and other local languages.
CAF.highlight: Terrain: vast, flat to rolling plateau; scattered hills in northeast and southwest; highest point: Mont Ngaoui 1,410 m.

TCD.name: Chad
TCD.geographicScope: Chad profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TCD.relationship: Central Africa, south of Libya. Independent country.
TCD.languages: Arabic, French, Sara and many other languages.
TCD.highlight: Chad is the largest of Africa's 16 landlocked countries.

CHL.name: Chile
CHL.geographicScope: Chile profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CHL.relationship: Southern South America, bordering the South Pacific Ocean, between Argentina and Peru. Independent country.
CHL.languages: Spanish; Mapudungun, Aymara, Quechua and Rapa Nui are among the Indigenous languages.
CHL.highlight: Chile is the longest country north-to-south in the world, extending across 39 degrees of latitude.

COL.name: Colombia
COL.geographicScope: Colombia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
COL.relationship: Northern South America, bordering the Caribbean Sea, between Panama and Venezuela, and bordering the North Pacific Ocean, between Ecuador and Panama. Independent country.
COL.highlight: Only South American country with coastlines on both the North Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea.

COM.name: Comoros
COM.geographicScope: Comoros profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
COM.relationship: Southern Africa, group of islands at the northern mouth of the Mozambique Channel, about two-thirds of the way between northern Madagascar and northern Mozambique. Independent country.
COM.highlight: Important location at northern end of Mozambique Channel; the only Arab League country that lies entirely in the Southern Hemisphere.

COK.name: Cook Islands
COK.geographicScope: Cook Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
COK.relationship: Oceania, group of islands in the South Pacific Ocean, about halfway between Hawaii and New Zealand. Self-governing in free association with New Zealand.
COK.highlight: The northern Cook Islands are seven low-lying, sparsely populated, coral atolls; the southern Cook Islands, where most of the population lives, consist of eight elevated, fertile, volcanic isles, including the largest, Rarotonga, at 67 sq km.

CRI.name: Costa Rica
CRI.geographicScope: Costa Rica profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CRI.relationship: Central America, bordering both the Caribbean Sea and the North Pacific Ocean, between Nicaragua and Panama. Independent country.
CRI.highlight: Four volcanoes, two of them active, rise near the capital of San Jose in the center of the country; one of the volcanoes, Irazu, erupted destructively in 1963-65.

HRV.name: Croatia
HRV.geographicScope: Croatia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
HRV.relationship: Southeastern Europe, bordering the Adriatic Sea, between Bosnia and Herzegovina and Slovenia. Independent country.
HRV.languages: Croatian; Serbian, Bosnian, Romani, Albanian and Italian minorities.
HRV.highlight: Croatia’s Adriatic coast is fringed by a large number of islands, islets and reefs.

CUB.name: Cuba
CUB.geographicScope: Cuba profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CUB.relationship: Caribbean, island between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, 150 km south of Key West, Florida. Independent country.
CUB.highlight: Largest country in Caribbean and westernmost island of the Greater Antilles.

CUW.name: Curaçao
CUW.geographicScope: Curaçao profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CUW.relationship: Caribbean, an island in the Caribbean Sea, 55 km off the coast of Venezuela. One of four constituent countries of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
CUW.languages: Papiamento, Dutch and English; Spanish is also spoken.
CUW.highlight: Curaçao has generally low, hilly terrain; Mount Christoffel rises to 372 metres.

CYP.name: Cyprus
CYP.geographicScope: Republic of Cyprus government-controlled area only for population; northern Cyprus is a separate map entity and is not included in the CYSTAT figure.
CYP.relationship: Republic of Cyprus, an independent country on an eastern Mediterranean island south of Turkey; the Turkish Cypriot-administered north is mapped separately.
CYP.languages: Greek and Turkish; English and other languages are also spoken.

population.note: Government-controlled area only: CYSTAT estimates 966,400 at end-2023 and 983,000 at end-2024.

CYP.highlight: The third largest island in the Mediterranean Sea (after Sicily and Sardinia).

CZE.name: Czech Republic
CZE.geographicScope: Czech Republic profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CZE.relationship: Central Europe, between Germany, Poland, Slovakia, and Austria. Independent country.
CZE.languages: Czech and Slovak, among other languages.
CZE.highlight: Landlocked; strategically located on some of oldest and most significant land routes in Europe; Moravian Gate is a traditional military corridor between the North European Plain and the Danube in central Europe.

COD.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
COD.geographicScope: Democratic Republic of the Congo profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
COD.relationship: Central Africa, northeast of Angola. Independent country.
COD.languages: French, Lingala, Swahili, Kikongo and Tshiluba.
COD.highlight: Second-largest country in Africa (after Algeria) and largest country in sub-Saharan Africa.

DNK.name: Denmark
DNK.geographicScope: Denmark proper, excluding Greenland and the Faroe Islands, which have separate map entries and population profiles.
DNK.relationship: Northern Europe, bordering the Baltic Sea and the North Sea, on a peninsula north of Germany (Jutland); also includes several major islands (Sjaelland, Fyn, and Bornholm). Independent country.
DNK.languages: Danish; English is a common second language, and German is spoken by a minority.
DNK.highlight: Composed of the Jutland Peninsula and a group of more than 400 islands (Danish Archipelago); controls Danish Straits (Skagerrak and Kattegat) linking Baltic and North Seas; about one-quarter of the population lives in greater Copenhagen.

DJI.name: Djibouti
DJI.geographicScope: Djibouti profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
DJI.relationship: Eastern Africa, bordering the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea, between Eritrea and Somalia. Independent country.
DJI.highlight: Lake Assal occupies Africa’s lowest land depression; coastal plains and plateaus are separated by mountains.

DMA.name: Dominica
DMA.geographicScope: Dominica profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
DMA.relationship: Caribbean, island between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, about halfway between Puerto Rico and Trinidad and Tobago. Independent country.
DMA.highlight: Known as "The Nature Island of the Caribbean" due to its lush and varied flora and fauna, which are protected by an extensive natural park system.

DOM.name: Dominican Republic
DOM.geographicScope: Dominican Republic profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
DOM.relationship: Caribbean, eastern two-thirds of the island of Hispaniola, between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, east of Haiti. Independent country.
DOM.highlight: Shares island of Hispaniola with Haiti (eastern two-thirds makes up the Dominican Republic, western one-third is Haiti).

TLS.name: East Timor
TLS.geographicScope: East Timor profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TLS.relationship: Independent country comprising eastern Timor, the Oecussi exclave and nearby islands; it shares Timor with Indonesia, northwest of Australia.
TLS.languages: Tetun, Mambai, Makasai and other local languages; Portuguese is also an official language.
TLS.highlight: The island of Timor is part of the Malay Archipelago and is the largest and easternmost of the Lesser Sunda Islands; the district of Oecussi is an exclave separated from Timor-Leste proper by Indonesia; Timor-Leste is the only Asian country located completely in the Southern Hemisphere.

ECU.name: Ecuador
ECU.geographicScope: Ecuador profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ECU.relationship: Western South America, bordering the Pacific Ocean at the Equator, between Colombia and Peru. Independent country.
ECU.languages: Spanish; Quechua and other Indigenous languages.
ECU.highlight: Ecuador’s landscape includes a coastal plain, Andean highlands and eastern Amazonian forest; Cotopaxi is an active Andean volcano.

EGY.name: Egypt
EGY.geographicScope: Egypt profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
EGY.relationship: Northern Africa, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, between Libya and the Gaza Strip, and the Red Sea north of Sudan, and includes the Asian Sinai Peninsula. Independent country.
EGY.languages: Arabic; English and French are also used.
EGY.highlight: The Sinai Peninsula connects Africa and Asia; the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and Red Sea shipping routes.

SLV.name: El Salvador
SLV.geographicScope: El Salvador profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SLV.relationship: Central America, bordering the North Pacific Ocean, between Guatemala and Honduras. Independent country.
SLV.languages: Spanish; Nawat is spoken by some Indigenous people.
SLV.highlight: Smallest Central American country and only one without a coastline on the Caribbean Sea.

GNQ.name: Equatorial Guinea
GNQ.geographicScope: Equatorial Guinea profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GNQ.relationship: Central Africa, bordering the Bight of Biafra, between Cameroon and Gabon. Independent country.
GNQ.languages: Spanish, Fang, Bubi, French, Portuguese and Fa d’Ambo.
GNQ.highlight: Insular and continental regions widely separated; despite its name, no part of the equator passes through Equatorial Guinea -- the mainland part of the country is located just north of the equator.

ERI.name: Eritrea
ERI.geographicScope: Eritrea profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ERI.relationship: Eastern Africa, bordering the Red Sea, between Djibouti and Sudan. Independent country.
ERI.languages: Tigrinya, Tigre, Arabic, English, Kunama, Afar and other languages.
ERI.highlight: The highlands descend eastward to a coastal desert plain along the Red Sea.

EST.name: Estonia
EST.geographicScope: Estonia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
EST.relationship: Eastern Europe, bordering the Baltic Sea and Gulf of Finland, between Latvia and Russia. Independent country.
EST.languages: Estonian and Russian, among other languages.
EST.highlight: The mainland terrain is flat, boggy, and partly wooded; over 1,500 islands lie offshore.

SWZ.name: Eswatini
SWZ.geographicScope: Eswatini profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SWZ.relationship: Southern Africa, between Mozambique and South Africa. Independent country.
SWZ.highlight: Landlocked; almost completely surrounded by South Africa.

ETH.name: Ethiopia
ETH.geographicScope: Ethiopia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ETH.relationship: Eastern Africa, west of Somalia. Independent country.
ETH.languages: Oromo, Amharic, Somali, Tigrinya, Sidamo, Afar and many other languages.
ETH.highlight: The most populous landlocked country in the world; the Blue Nile, the chief headstream of the Nile by water volume, rises in T'ana Hayk (Lake Tana) in northwest Ethiopia.

FLK.name: Falkland Islands
FLK.geographicScope: Falkland Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
FLK.relationship: UK-administered overseas territory in the South Atlantic, east of Argentina; sovereignty is also claimed by Argentina.
FLK.highlight: Deeply indented coast provides good natural harbors; short growing season.

FRO.name: Faroe Islands
FRO.geographicScope: Faroe Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
FRO.relationship: Self-governing island group within the Kingdom of Denmark, between Iceland and Norway in the North Atlantic.
FRO.highlight: Archipelago of 17 inhabited islands, one uninhabited island, and a few uninhabited islets; strategically located along important sea lanes in northeastern Atlantic; precipitous terrain limits habitation to small coastal lowlands.

FSM.name: Federated States of Micronesia
FSM.geographicScope: Federated States of Micronesia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
FSM.relationship: Independent federal republic in free association with the United States, comprising four major island groups in the western Pacific.
FSM.languages: English, Chuukese, Kosraean, Pohnpeian, Yapese and other island languages.
FSM.highlight: Composed of four major island groups totaling 607 islands.

FJI.name: Fiji
FJI.geographicScope: Fiji profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
FJI.relationship: Oceania, island group in the South Pacific Ocean, about two-thirds of the way from Hawaii to New Zealand. Independent country.
FJI.highlight: Consists of 332 islands, approximately 110 of which are inhabited, and more than 500 islets.

FIN.name: Finland
FIN.geographicScope: Finland’s national population profile includes autonomous Åland, although Åland is a separate map entry; these populations must not be added together.
FIN.relationship: Independent country in northern Europe, between Sweden and Russia; autonomous Åland is part of Finland but mapped separately.
FIN.languages: Finnish and Swedish; Russian and other languages are also spoken.

population.note: National estimate includes the separately mapped Åland.

FIN.highlight: Finland’s mostly low, rolling terrain is interspersed with lakes and small hills.

FRA.name: France
FRA.geographicScope: Metropolitan France including Corsica, plus French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte and Réunion. Other separately mapped French collectivities have their own cards.
FRA.relationship: Independent country centred in western Europe, with overseas regions in South America, the Caribbean and the Indian Ocean.
FRA.languages: French; regional languages and overseas languages include Breton, Corsican, Basque, Creoles and Mahorian.
FRA.highlight: The Seine and Loire flow toward the Atlantic, while the Rhône flows south to the Mediterranean.

PYF.name: French Polynesia
PYF.geographicScope: French Polynesia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PYF.relationship: French overseas collectivity of five archipelagos in the South Pacific, between Australia and South America.
PYF.languages: French, Tahitian, Marquesan, Austral languages and Paumotu.
PYF.highlight: Includes five archipelagoes: four volcanic (Iles Gambier, Iles Marquises, Iles Tubuai, Society Islands) and one coral (Archipel des Tuamotu).

ATF.name: French Southern and Antarctic Lands
ATF.geographicScope: At this map scale the feature shows Kerguelen and part of Crozet. The source profile also covers other southern and scattered Indian Ocean islands; the Antarctic claim is outside the quiz.
ATF.relationship: French-administered territory of remote southern Indian Ocean islands; Antarctic claims are not shown in this quiz.
ATF.languages: No permanent resident language community; the source does not enumerate research-station languages.

population.period: No dated resident-population series in the archived source.
population.note: The archived source reports no permanent inhabitants; temporary personnel are not a resident population.

ATF.highlight: The Kerguelen Islands have a rugged interior of mountains and valleys; Crozet is another remote southern Indian Ocean archipelago.

GAB.name: Gabon
GAB.geographicScope: Gabon profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GAB.relationship: Central Africa, bordering the Atlantic Ocean at the Equator, between Republic of the Congo and Equatorial Guinea. Independent country.
GAB.languages: French, Fang, Myene, Nzebi, Bapounou and other languages.
GAB.highlight: A narrow coastal plain gives way to a hilly interior, with savanna in the east and south.

GEO.name: Georgia
GEO.geographicScope: National Georgia profile, not a census reconciled to the map’s disputed de facto boundaries in Abkhazia and South Ossetia.
GEO.relationship: Independent country in the Caucasus, east of the Black Sea between Russia and Turkey; territorial control is disputed in Abkhazia and South Ossetia.
GEO.languages: Georgian; Azerbaijani, Armenian, Russian and Abkhaz are also spoken.
GEO.highlight: The Greater Caucasus lies in the north, the Lesser Caucasus in the south, and western lowlands open onto the Black Sea.

DEU.name: Germany
DEU.geographicScope: Germany profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
DEU.relationship: Central Europe, bordering the Baltic Sea and the North Sea, between the Netherlands and Poland, south of Denmark. Independent country.
DEU.languages: German; Danish, Frisian, Sorbian, Romani and other minority languages.
DEU.highlight: The Rhine, Weser, Oder and Elbe flow northward, while the Danube begins in the Black Forest and flows eastward.

GHA.name: Ghana
GHA.geographicScope: Ghana profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GHA.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the Gulf of Guinea, between Cote d'Ivoire and Togo. Independent country.
GHA.languages: Akan varieties including Asante and Fante, Ewe, Dagbani, Ga and other languages; English is used in government.
GHA.highlight: Lake Volta is the world's largest artificial lake (manmade reservoir) by surface area (8,482 sq km; 3,275 sq mi); the lake was created after the Akosombo Dam was completed in 1965.

GRC.name: Greece
GRC.geographicScope: Greece profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GRC.relationship: Southern Europe, bordering the Aegean Sea, Ionian Sea, and the Mediterranean Sea, between Albania and Turkey. Independent country.
GRC.languages: Greek; English and French are also spoken.
GRC.highlight: Greece combines a mountainous peninsula with a large archipelago in the Aegean and Ionian seas.

GRL.name: Greenland
GRL.geographicScope: Greenland profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GRL.relationship: Self-governing part of the Kingdom of Denmark, between the Arctic and North Atlantic oceans, northeast of Canada.
GRL.highlight: An ice sheet covers most of Greenland, leaving a narrow, mountainous, rocky coastal fringe.

GRD.name: Grenada
GRD.geographicScope: Grenada profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GRD.relationship: Caribbean, island between the Caribbean Sea and Atlantic Ocean, north of Trinidad and Tobago. Independent country.
GRD.highlight: Terrain: volcanic in origin with central mountains; highest point: Mount Saint Catherine 840 m.

GUM.name: Guam
GUM.geographicScope: Guam profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GUM.relationship: US territory in the western North Pacific, the southernmost island of the Mariana chain.
GUM.languages: English, Chamorro, Filipino and other Pacific and Asian languages.
GUM.highlight: Largest and southernmost island in the Mariana Islands archipelago and the largest island in Micronesia; strategic location in western North Pacific Ocean.

GTM.name: Guatemala
GTM.geographicScope: Guatemala profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GTM.relationship: Central America, bordering the North Pacific Ocean, between El Salvador and Mexico, and bordering the Gulf of Honduras (Caribbean Sea) between Honduras and Belize. Independent country.
GTM.languages: Spanish; Maya languages including Q’eqchi’, K’iche’, Mam and Kaqchikel; Xinca and Garifuna.
GTM.highlight: Despite having both eastern and western coastlines (Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean), there are no natural harbors on the west coast.

GGY.name: Guernsey
GGY.geographicScope: Bailiwick of Guernsey, including its associated islands; not the United Kingdom’s population.
GGY.relationship: Self-governing British Crown dependency in the Channel Islands, off the coast of France; not part of the United Kingdom.
GGY.languages: English, French and a local Norman language.
GGY.highlight: Terrain: mostly flat with low hills in southwest; highest point: Le Moulin on Sark 114 m.

GIN.name: Guinea
GIN.geographicScope: Guinea profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GIN.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Guinea-Bissau and Sierra Leone. Independent country.
GIN.languages: French, Pular, Maninka, Susu and other languages.
GIN.highlight: The Niger and its important tributary, the Milo River, have their sources in the Guinean highlands.

GNB.name: Guinea-Bissau
GNB.geographicScope: Guinea-Bissau profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GNB.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Guinea and Senegal. Independent country.
GNB.languages: Guinea-Bissau Creole, Portuguese, Pular and Mandingo.
GNB.highlight: This small country is swampy along its western coast and is low-lying inland.

GUY.name: Guyana
GUY.geographicScope: Guyana profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GUY.relationship: Northern South America, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Suriname and Venezuela. Independent country.
GUY.languages: English, Guyanese Creole, Indigenous languages and Caribbean Hindustani.
GUY.highlight: The third-smallest country in South America after Suriname and Uruguay; contains some of the largest unspoiled rainforests on the continent.

HTI.name: Haiti
HTI.geographicScope: Haiti profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
HTI.relationship: Caribbean, western one-third of the island of Hispaniola, between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, west of the Dominican Republic. Independent country.
HTI.highlight: Shares island of Hispaniola with Dominican Republic (western one-third is Haiti, eastern two-thirds is the Dominican Republic); it is the most mountainous nation in the Caribbean.

HMD.name: Heard Island and McDonald Islands
HMD.geographicScope: Heard Island and McDonald Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
HMD.relationship: Islands in the Indian Ocean, about two-thirds of the way from Madagascar to Antarctica. Territory of Australia.

population.period: No dated resident-population series in the archived source.
population.note: The archived source reports no permanent inhabitants; temporary personnel are not a resident population.

HMD.highlight: Heard Island is dominated by the Big Ben massif and the active Mawson Peak volcano, which reaches 2,745 metres.

HND.name: Honduras
HND.geographicScope: Honduras profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
HND.relationship: Central America, bordering the Caribbean Sea, between Guatemala and Nicaragua and bordering the Gulf of Fonseca (North Pacific Ocean), between El Salvador and Nicaragua. Independent country.
HND.highlight: Mountainous interior terrain contrasts with narrow coastal plains and a much longer Caribbean than Pacific coast.

HKG.name: Hong Kong
HKG.geographicScope: Hong Kong special administrative region only, not mainland China or Macao.
HKG.relationship: Special administrative region of China on the South China Sea coast, beside Guangdong province.
HKG.languages: Cantonese, English, Mandarin and other Chinese languages.
HKG.highlight: Consists of a mainland area (the New Territories) and over 200 islands.

HUN.name: Hungary
HUN.geographicScope: Hungary profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
HUN.relationship: Central Europe, northwest of Romania. Independent country.
HUN.languages: Hungarian; English, German and other languages are also spoken.
HUN.highlight: The Danube and Tisza rivers divide much of Hungary’s lowland landscape into distinct regions.

ISL.name: Iceland
ISL.geographicScope: Iceland profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ISL.relationship: Northern Europe, island between the Greenland Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, northwest of the United Kingdom. Independent country.
ISL.languages: Icelandic; English, Polish and other Nordic languages are also spoken.
ISL.highlight: Strategic location between Greenland and Europe; westernmost European country; Reykjavik is the northernmost national capital in the world; more land covered by glaciers than in all of continental Europe.

IND.name: India
IND.geographicScope: India profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
IND.relationship: Southern Asia, bordering the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, between Burma and Pakistan. Independent country.
IND.languages: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati, Urdu and many other languages; English is widely used in public life.
IND.highlight: Dominates South Asian subcontinent; near important Indian Ocean trade routes; Kanchenjunga, third tallest mountain in the world, lies on the border with Nepal.

IDN.name: Indonesia
IDN.geographicScope: Indonesia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
IDN.relationship: Southeastern Asia, archipelago between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific Ocean. Independent country.
IDN.languages: Indonesian; Javanese and hundreds of other local languages.
IDN.highlight: 13,466 islands are in the archipelago, of which 922 are permanently inhabited; Indonesia is the world's largest country composed solely of islands; the country straddles the equator and occupies a strategic location along major sea lanes from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific Ocean.

IRN.name: Iran
IRN.geographicScope: Iran profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
IRN.relationship: Middle East, bordering the Gulf of Oman, the Persian Gulf, and the Caspian Sea, between Iraq and Pakistan. Independent country.
IRN.languages: Persian, Azerbaijani, Kurdish, Gilaki, Mazandarani, Luri, Balochi and Arabic.
IRN.highlight: A rugged mountain rim surrounds high interior basins and deserts; Damavand is a prominent volcanic peak.

IRQ.name: Iraq
IRQ.geographicScope: Iraq profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
IRQ.relationship: Middle East, bordering the Persian Gulf, between Iran and Kuwait. Independent country.
IRQ.languages: Arabic and Kurdish; Turkmen and Syriac (Neo-Aramaic) are also spoken.
IRQ.highlight: Broad plains and southern marshes contrast with mountains along the borders with Iran and Turkey.

IRL.name: Ireland
IRL.geographicScope: Ireland profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
IRL.relationship: Western Europe, occupying five-sixths of the island of Ireland in the North Atlantic Ocean, west of Great Britain. Independent country.
IRL.highlight: Strategic location on major air and sea routes between North America and northern Europe; over 40% of the population resides within 100 km of Dublin.

IMN.name: Isle of Man
IMN.geographicScope: Isle of Man Crown dependency only, not the United Kingdom.
IMN.relationship: Self-governing British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea, between Great Britain and Ireland; not part of the United Kingdom.
IMN.languages: English; Manx Gaelic is known by a small minority.
IMN.highlight: One small islet, the Calf of Man, lies to the southwest and is a bird sanctuary.

ISR.name: Israel
ISR.geographicScope: Israel source profile. Its treatment of East Jerusalem, the Golan Heights and settlers does not exactly define the map polygons; inclusion is not a statement of recognition.
ISR.relationship: Country on the eastern Mediterranean between Lebanon and Egypt; the map and source reflect disputed territorial boundaries, not a recognition policy.
ISR.languages: Hebrew and Arabic; English is widely used as a foreign language.

population.note: Archived estimate; source treatment of disputed areas and settlers is not reconciled to map polygons.

ISR.highlight: The Negev Desert in the south contrasts with coastal plains, central hills and the Jordan Rift Valley.

ITA.name: Italy
ITA.geographicScope: Italy profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ITA.relationship: Southern Europe, a peninsula extending into the central Mediterranean Sea, northeast of Tunisia. Independent country.
ITA.languages: Italian; German, French, Slovene and Croatian minorities.
ITA.highlight: Much of Italy is rugged and mountainous, with plains and coastal lowlands around its Mediterranean peninsula.

CIV.name: Ivory Coast
CIV.geographicScope: Ivory Coast profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CIV.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Ghana and Liberia. Independent country.
CIV.languages: French; Dioula and many other local languages.
CIV.highlight: Most of the inhabitants live along the sandy coastal region; apart from the capital area, the forested interior is sparsely populated.

JAM.name: Jamaica
JAM.geographicScope: Jamaica profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
JAM.relationship: Caribbean, island in the Caribbean Sea, south of Cuba. Independent country.
JAM.highlight: Third largest island in the Caribbean (after Cuba and Hispaniola); strategic location between Cayman Trench and Jamaica Channel, the main sea lanes for the Panama Canal.

JPN.name: Japan
JPN.geographicScope: Japan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
JPN.relationship: Eastern Asia, island chain between the North Pacific Ocean and the Sea of Japan, east of the Korean Peninsula. Independent country.
JPN.highlight: Strategic location in northeast Asia; composed of four main islands (the "Home Islands") -- Hokkaido, Honshu (the largest, most populous, and site of Tokyo, the capital), Shikoku, and Kyushu.

JEY.name: Jersey
JEY.geographicScope: Bailiwick of Jersey only, not the United Kingdom’s population.
JEY.relationship: Self-governing British Crown dependency in the Channel Islands, near France; not part of the United Kingdom.
JEY.highlight: Largest and southernmost of Channel Islands; about 30% of population concentrated in Saint Helier.

JOR.name: Jordan
JOR.geographicScope: Jordan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
JOR.relationship: Middle East, northwest of Saudi Arabia, between Israel (to the west) and Iraq. Independent country.
JOR.languages: Arabic; English is also widely understood.
JOR.highlight: The Jordan Rift Valley contains the Jordan River and Dead Sea, contrasting with the country’s arid plateau.

KAZ.name: Kazakhstan
KAZ.geographicScope: Kazakhstan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
KAZ.relationship: Central Asia, northwest of China; a small portion west of the Ural (Oral) River in easternmost Europe. Independent country.
KAZ.highlight: Kazakhstan is the world’s largest landlocked country and stretches across both sides of the Ural River region.

KEN.name: Kenya
KEN.geographicScope: Kenya profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
KEN.relationship: Eastern Africa, bordering the Indian Ocean, between Somalia and Tanzania. Independent country.
KEN.languages: Swahili, English and numerous Indigenous languages.
KEN.highlight: The Great Rift Valley cuts through Kenya’s central highlands; Mount Kenya reaches 5,199 metres.

KIR.name: Kiribati
KIR.geographicScope: Kiribati profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
KIR.relationship: Oceania, group of 32 coral atolls and one raised coral island in the Pacific Ocean, straddling the Equator; the capital Tarawa is about halfway between Hawaii and Australia. Independent country.
KIR.highlight: Terrain: mostly low-lying coral atolls surrounded by extensive reefs; highest point: unnamed elevation on Banaba 81 m.

KOS.name: Kosovo
KOS.geographicScope: Kosovo profile only; shown separately from Serbia under the map policy, without implying universal recognition.
KOS.relationship: Self-governing state in the Balkans, bordering Serbia and North Macedonia; it declared independence in 2008, but recognition is not universal and Serbia claims it.
KOS.languages: Albanian and Serbian; Bosnian, Turkish and Romani are also spoken.
KOS.highlight: The Nerodimka River has branches draining toward different seas, one through the Danube system to the Black Sea.

KWT.name: Kuwait
KWT.geographicScope: Kuwait profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
KWT.relationship: Middle East, bordering the Persian Gulf, between Iraq and Saudi Arabia. Independent country.
KWT.highlight: Terrain: flat to slightly undulating desert plain; highest point: 3.6 km W. of Al-Salmi Border Post 300 m.

KGZ.name: Kyrgyzstan
KGZ.geographicScope: Kyrgyzstan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
KGZ.relationship: Central Asia, west of China, south of Kazakhstan. Independent country.
KGZ.highlight: Landlocked; entirely mountainous, dominated by the Tien Shan range; 94% of the country is 1,000 m above sea level with an average elevation of 2,750 m; many tall peaks, glaciers, and high-altitude lakes.

LAO.name: Laos
LAO.geographicScope: Laos profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LAO.relationship: Southeastern Asia, northeast of Thailand, west of Vietnam. Independent country.
LAO.languages: Lao; French, English and numerous ethnic-community languages.
LAO.highlight: Landlocked; most of the country is mountainous and thickly forested; the Mekong River forms a large part of the western boundary with Thailand.

LVA.name: Latvia
LVA.geographicScope: Latvia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LVA.relationship: Eastern Europe, bordering the Baltic Sea, between Estonia and Lithuania. Independent country.
LVA.languages: Latvian and Russian; Polish, Ukrainian and Belarusian minorities.
LVA.highlight: Most of the country is composed of fertile low-lying plains with some hills in the east.

LBN.name: Lebanon
LBN.geographicScope: Lebanon profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LBN.relationship: Middle East, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, between Israel and Syria. Independent country.
LBN.highlight: The Bekaa Valley separates the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon mountain ranges.

LSO.name: Lesotho
LSO.geographicScope: Lesotho profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LSO.relationship: Southern Africa, an enclave of South Africa. Independent country.
LSO.languages: Sesotho and English; Phuthi, Xhosa and Zulu are also spoken.
LSO.highlight: Landlocked, surrounded by South Africa; mountainous, more than 80% of the country is 1,800 m (5,900 ft) above sea level.

LBR.name: Liberia
LBR.geographicScope: Liberia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LBR.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Cote d'Ivoire and Sierra Leone. Independent country.
LBR.languages: English, Liberian English varieties and many Indigenous languages.
LBR.highlight: Facing the Atlantic Ocean, the coastline is characterized by lagoons, mangrove swamps, and river-deposited sandbars; the inland grassy plateau supports limited agriculture.

LBY.name: Libya
LBY.geographicScope: Libya profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LBY.relationship: Northern Africa, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, between Egypt, Tunisia, and Algeria. Independent country.
LBY.languages: Arabic and Tamazight varieties; Italian and English are also used.
LBY.highlight: More than 90% of the country is desert or semidesert.

LIE.name: Liechtenstein
LIE.geographicScope: Liechtenstein profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LIE.relationship: Central Europe, between Austria and Switzerland. Independent country.
LIE.languages: German, especially Alemannic varieties; Italian, Turkish and Portuguese minorities.
LIE.highlight: Along with Uzbekistan, one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world; variety of microclimatic variations based on elevation.

LTU.name: Lithuania
LTU.geographicScope: Lithuania profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LTU.relationship: Eastern Europe, bordering the Baltic Sea, between Latvia and Russia, west of Belarus. Independent country.
LTU.highlight: Fertile central plains are separated by hilly uplands that are ancient glacial deposits.

LUX.name: Luxembourg
LUX.geographicScope: Luxembourg profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LUX.relationship: Western Europe, between France and Germany. Independent country.
LUX.highlight: Terrain: mostly gently rolling uplands with broad, shallow valleys; uplands to slightly mountainous in the north; steep slope down to Moselle flood plain in the southeast; highest point: Buurgplaatz 559 m.

MAC.name: Macau
MAC.geographicScope: Macao special administrative region only, not mainland China or Hong Kong.
MAC.relationship: Special administrative region of China on the Pearl River estuary, across from Hong Kong.
MAC.languages: Cantonese, Mandarin, Portuguese, English and other languages.
MAC.highlight: Primarily urban; an area of land reclaimed from the sea measuring 5.2 sq km (2 sq mi) and known as Cotai now connects the islands of Coloane and Taipa; the island area is connected to the mainland peninsula by three bridges.

MDG.name: Madagascar
MDG.geographicScope: Madagascar profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MDG.relationship: Southern Africa, island in the Indian Ocean, east of Mozambique. Independent country.
MDG.languages: Malagasy and French; English is also spoken.
MDG.highlight: Terrain: narrow coastal plain, high plateau and mountains in center; highest point: Maromokotro 2,876 m.

MWI.name: Malawi
MWI.geographicScope: Malawi profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MWI.relationship: Southern Africa, east of Zambia, west and north of Mozambique. Independent country.
MWI.languages: Chewa and English; Tumbuka, Yao, Lomwe, Sena and other languages.
MWI.highlight: Landlocked; Lake Nyasa, about 580 km (360 mi) long, is the country's most prominent physical feature; it contains more fish species than any other lake on earth.

MYS.name: Malaysia
MYS.geographicScope: Malaysia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MYS.relationship: Southeastern Asia, peninsula bordering Thailand and northern one-third of the island of Borneo, bordering Indonesia, Brunei, and the South China Sea, south of Vietnam. Independent country.
MYS.languages: Malay, English, Chinese languages and Tamil, among other languages.
MYS.highlight: Coastal plains rise into hills and mountains; Mount Kinabalu reaches 4,095 metres.

MDV.name: Maldives
MDV.geographicScope: Maldives profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MDV.relationship: Southern Asia, group of atolls in the Indian Ocean, south-southwest of India. Independent country.
MDV.highlight: Smallest Asian country; archipelago of 1,190 coral islands grouped into 26 atolls (200 inhabited islands, plus 80 islands with tourist resorts); strategic location along major sea lanes in Indian Ocean.

MLI.name: Mali
MLI.geographicScope: Mali profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MLI.relationship: Interior Western Africa, southwest of Algeria, north of Guinea, Cote d'Ivoire, and Burkina Faso, west of Niger. Independent country.
MLI.languages: Bambara, Fulani, Dogon, Soninke, Malinke, Songhai, Tamasheq, French and other languages.
MLI.highlight: Landlocked; divided into three natural zones: the southern, cultivated Sudanese; the central, semiarid Sahelian; and the northern, arid Saharan.

MLT.name: Malta
MLT.geographicScope: Malta profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MLT.relationship: Southern Europe, islands in the Mediterranean Sea, south of Sicily (Italy). Independent country.
MLT.highlight: The country is an archipelago, with only the three largest islands (Malta, Ghawdex or Gozo, and Kemmuna or Comino) inhabited; numerous bays provide good harbors.

MHL.name: Marshall Islands
MHL.geographicScope: Marshall Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MHL.relationship: Independent Pacific island country in free association with the United States; its atolls form the Ratak and Ralik chains.
MHL.highlight: Low coral atolls and sand islands form two roughly parallel chains, Ratak and Ralik.

MRT.name: Mauritania
MRT.geographicScope: Mauritania profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MRT.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Senegal and Western Sahara. Independent country.
MRT.languages: Arabic, Pular, Soninke, Wolof and French.
MRT.highlight: Mauritania spans the Saharan and Sahelian zones, with many settlements concentrated along the Senegal River and Atlantic coast.

MUS.name: Mauritius
MUS.geographicScope: Mauritius profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MUS.relationship: Southern Africa, island in the Indian Ocean, about 800 km (500 mi) east of Madagascar. Independent country.
MUS.languages: Mauritian Creole, Bhojpuri, French and English.
MUS.highlight: The main island is volcanic and largely ringed by coral reefs; it was home to the now-extinct dodo.

MEX.name: Mexico
MEX.geographicScope: Mexico profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MEX.relationship: North America, bordering the Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America, between Belize and the United States and bordering the North Pacific Ocean, between Guatemala and the United States. Independent country.
MEX.languages: Spanish; Nahuatl, Maya languages and other Indigenous languages.
MEX.highlight: Strategic location on southern border of the US; Mexico is one of the countries along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes.

MDA.name: Moldova
MDA.geographicScope: Moldova profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MDA.relationship: Eastern Europe, northeast of Romania. Independent country.
MDA.languages: Romanian, Russian, Gagauz, Ukrainian, Bulgarian and Romani.
MDA.highlight: Landlocked; has many types of sedimentary rocks and minerals, including sand, gravel, gypsum, and limestone.

MCO.name: Monaco
MCO.geographicScope: Monaco profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MCO.relationship: Western Europe, bordering the Mediterranean Sea on the southern coast of France, near the border with Italy. Independent country.
MCO.highlight: Second-smallest independent state in the world (after the Holy See); smallest country with a coastline; almost entirely urban.

MNG.name: Mongolia
MNG.geographicScope: Mongolia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MNG.relationship: Northern Asia, between China and Russia. Independent country.
MNG.languages: Mongolian, especially Khalkha; Turkic languages and Russian are also spoken.
MNG.highlight: Grassland steppe and mountain ranges contrast with the Gobi Desert in the south.

MNE.name: Montenegro
MNE.geographicScope: Montenegro profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MNE.relationship: Southeastern Europe, between the Adriatic Sea and Serbia. Independent country.
MNE.highlight: Terrain: highly indented coastline with narrow coastal plain backed by rugged high limestone mountains and plateaus; highest point: Zia Kolata 2,534 m.

MSR.name: Montserrat
MSR.geographicScope: Montserrat profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MSR.relationship: Caribbean, island in the Caribbean Sea, southeast of Puerto Rico. Overseas territory of the UK.
MSR.highlight: The island is entirely volcanic in origin and composed of three major volcanic centers of differing ages.

MAR.name: Morocco
MAR.geographicScope: Morocco is mapped separately from Western Sahara; the archived Morocco profile follows a different territorial policy after 2020 and does not establish a polygon-matched population.
MAR.relationship: Independent country in northwestern Africa on the Atlantic and Mediterranean; Western Sahara is disputed and mapped separately.

population.note: Archived national estimate; source treatment of Western Sahara differs from this map and is not separately quantified.

MAR.highlight: Strategic location along Strait of Gibraltar; the only African nation to have both Atlantic and Mediterranean coastlines; the waters off the Atlantic coast are particularly rich fishing areas.

MOZ.name: Mozambique
MOZ.geographicScope: Mozambique profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MOZ.relationship: Southeastern Africa, bordering the Mozambique Channel, between South Africa and Tanzania. Independent country.
MOZ.languages: Makhuwa, Portuguese, Tsonga, Nyanja, Sena, Lomwe and other languages.
MOZ.highlight: The Zambezi River flows through the north-central and most fertile part of the country.

MMR.name: Myanmar
MMR.geographicScope: Myanmar profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MMR.relationship: Southeastern Asia, bordering the Andaman Sea and the Bay of Bengal, between Bangladesh and Thailand. Independent country.
MMR.highlight: Strategic location near major Indian Ocean shipping lanes; the north-south flowing Irrawaddy River is the country's largest and most important commercial waterway.

NAM.name: Namibia
NAM.geographicScope: Namibia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
NAM.relationship: Southern Africa, bordering the South Atlantic Ocean, between Angola and South Africa. Independent country.
NAM.languages: Oshiwambo languages, Nama/Damara, Kavango languages, Afrikaans, Herero and English, among others.
NAM.highlight: The Namib Desert, after which the country is named, is considered to be the oldest desert in the world; some 14% of the land is protected, including virtually the entire Namib Desert coastal strip.

NRU.name: Nauru
NRU.geographicScope: Nauru profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
NRU.relationship: Oceania, island in the South Pacific Ocean, south of the Marshall Islands. Independent country.
NRU.languages: Nauruan and English; Gilbertese and Chinese are also spoken.
NRU.highlight: Nauru is the third-smallest country in the world behind the Holy See (Vatican City) and Monaco.

NPL.name: Nepal
NPL.geographicScope: Nepal profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
NPL.relationship: Southern Asia, between China and India. Independent country.
NPL.languages: Nepali, Maithili, Bhojpuri, Tharu, Tamang, Bajjika and many other languages.
NPL.highlight: The landscape rises from the southern Tarai plain to the Himalayas, including Mount Everest on the border with China.

NLD.name: Netherlands
NLD.geographicScope: Map includes the European Netherlands and Caribbean municipalities Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba. The source’s Netherlands population is not itemized by those islands; Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten are separate profiles.
NLD.relationship: Constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, including European and Caribbean municipalities; Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten are separate constituent countries.
NLD.languages: Dutch and Frisian; English and Papiamento are used in the Caribbean Netherlands.
NLD.highlight: Located at mouths of three major European rivers (Rhine (Rijn), Meuse (Maas), and Scheldt (Schelde)); about a quarter of the country lies below sea level and only about half of the land exceeds one meter above sea level.

NCL.name: New Caledonia
NCL.geographicScope: New Caledonia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
NCL.relationship: Oceania, islands in the South Pacific Ocean, east of Australia. Special collectivity of France.
NCL.highlight: Consists of the main island of New Caledonia (one of the largest in the Pacific Ocean), the archipelago of Iles Loyauté, and numerous small, sparsely populated islands and atolls.

NZL.name: New Zealand
NZL.geographicScope: New Zealand national profile; Cook Islands and Niue are separately mapped self-governing states in free association, with their own population figures.
NZL.relationship: Oceania, islands in the South Pacific Ocean, southeast of Australia. Independent country.
NZL.languages: English, Māori and New Zealand Sign Language; Samoan and other community languages.
NZL.highlight: Consists of two main islands and a number of smaller islands.

NIC.name: Nicaragua
NIC.geographicScope: Nicaragua profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
NIC.relationship: Central America, bordering both the Caribbean Sea and the North Pacific Ocean, between Costa Rica and Honduras. Independent country.
NIC.highlight: Largest country in Central America; contains the largest freshwater body in Central America, Lago de Nicaragua.

NER.name: Niger
NER.geographicScope: Niger profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
NER.relationship: Western Africa, southeast of Algeria. Independent country.
NER.languages: Hausa, Zarma, Fulfulde, Tamasheq, Kanuri, French and other languages.
NER.highlight: Landlocked; one of the hottest countries in the world; northern four-fifths is desert, southern one-fifth is savanna that is suitable for livestock and limited agriculture.

NGA.name: Nigeria
NGA.geographicScope: Nigeria profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
NGA.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the Gulf of Guinea, between Benin and Cameroon. Independent country.
NGA.languages: English, Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, Fulani and hundreds of other languages.
NGA.highlight: The Niger River enters the country in the northwest and flows southward through tropical rainforests and swamps to its delta in the Gulf of Guinea.

NIU.name: Niue
NIU.geographicScope: Niue profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
NIU.relationship: Oceania, island in the South Pacific Ocean, east of Tonga. Self-governing in free association with New Zealand since 1974.
NIU.highlight: One of world's largest coral islands; the only major break in the surrounding coral reef occurs in the central western part of the coast.

NFK.name: Norfolk Island
NFK.geographicScope: Norfolk Island profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
NFK.relationship: Oceania, island in the South Pacific Ocean, east of Australia. Administered as a territory of Australia.
NFK.languages: English and Norf’k, a language with English and Tahitian roots.
NFK.highlight: Most of the 32-km (20-mi) coastline consists of almost inaccessible cliffs, but the land slopes down to the sea in one small southern area on Sydney Bay, where the capital of Kingston is located.

PRK.name: North Korea
PRK.geographicScope: North Korea profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PRK.relationship: Eastern Asia, northern half of the Korean Peninsula bordering the Korea Bay and the Sea of Japan, between China and South Korea. Independent country.
PRK.highlight: Strategic location bordering China, South Korea, and Russia; mountainous interior is isolated and sparsely populated.

MKD.name: North Macedonia
MKD.geographicScope: North Macedonia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MKD.relationship: Southeastern Europe, north of Greece. Independent country.
MKD.languages: Macedonian and Albanian; Turkish, Romani and other minority languages.
MKD.highlight: Landlocked; major transportation corridor from Western and Central Europe to Aegean Sea and Southern Europe to Western Europe.

MNP.name: Northern Mariana Islands
MNP.geographicScope: Northern Mariana Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
MNP.relationship: US commonwealth in the western North Pacific, comprising the northern islands of the Mariana chain.
MNP.languages: Chamorro, English, Carolinian, Philippine languages and other languages.
MNP.highlight: Terrain: the southern islands in this north-south trending archipelago are limestone, with fringing coral reefs; the northern islands are volcanic, with active volcanoes on several islands; highest point: Agrihan Volcano 965 m.

NOR.name: Norway
NOR.geographicScope: Map includes Norway, Svalbard and Jan Mayen. The displayed population is the Norway profile alone; Svalbard’s differently dated estimate is not silently added, and Jan Mayen has no permanent inhabitants.
NOR.relationship: Independent country in northern Europe, west of Sweden; the map also includes the Norwegian territories of Svalbard and Jan Mayen.
NOR.languages: Norwegian (Bokmål and Nynorsk written forms); Sami and Finnish minorities; Russian is also used in Svalbard.

population.note: Norway profile estimate only; the map also includes Svalbard and Jan Mayen. Different source years are not combined.

NOR.highlight: About two-thirds mountains; some 50,000 islands off its much-indented coastline; strategic location adjacent to sea lanes and air routes in North Atlantic; one of the most rugged and longest coastlines in the world.

OMN.name: Oman
OMN.geographicScope: Oman profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
OMN.relationship: Middle East, bordering the Arabian Sea, Gulf of Oman, and Persian Gulf, between Yemen and the UAE. Independent country.
OMN.languages: Arabic, English, Balochi, Swahili, Urdu and Indian languages.
OMN.highlight: Consists of Oman proper and two northern exclaves, Musandam and Al Madhah; the former is a peninsula that occupies a strategic location adjacent to the Strait of Hormuz.

PAK.name: Pakistan
PAK.geographicScope: Pakistan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PAK.relationship: Southern Asia, bordering the Arabian Sea, between India on the east and Iran and Afghanistan on the west and China in the north. Independent country.
PAK.languages: Punjabi, Pashto, Sindhi, Saraiki, Urdu, Balochi and other languages; English is also an official language.
PAK.highlight: The Khyber and Bolan passes have long connected routes between Central and South Asia.

PLW.name: Palau
PLW.geographicScope: Palau profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PLW.relationship: Independent island country in free association with the United States, in the western Caroline Islands east of the Philippines.
PLW.languages: Palauan and English; Filipino and other languages are also spoken.
PLW.highlight: Westernmost archipelago in the Caroline chain, consists of six island groups totaling more than 300 islands; includes world-famous Rock Islands.

PSX.name: Palestine
PSX.geographicScope: Palestinian population of the West Bank and Gaza Strip combined, using the PCBS revised estimate; not the population of Israel or of the worldwide Palestinian diaspora.
PSX.relationship: Palestinian territories in western Asia: the West Bank lies beside Jordan and Israel, and Gaza borders Egypt, Israel and the Mediterranean. Sovereignty and control are disputed.
PSX.languages: Arabic; Hebrew and English are also spoken.

population.period: No comparable revised whole-territory change series is identified alongside this end-2025 count.
population.note: PCBS revised end-2025 estimate. Older projections on the same page exclude wartime revisions for Gaza and are not used to infer a trend.

PSX.highlight: The West Bank has inland highlands, while Gaza is a narrow coastal strip on the Mediterranean.

PAN.name: Panama
PAN.geographicScope: Panama profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PAN.relationship: Central America, bordering both the Caribbean Sea and the North Pacific Ocean, between Colombia and Costa Rica. Independent country.
PAN.languages: Spanish; Indigenous languages including Ngäbere and Guna, English and creoles are also spoken.
PAN.highlight: Strategic location on eastern end of isthmus forming land bridge that connects North and South America; controls the Panama Canal, which links the North Atlantic Ocean with the North Pacific Ocean via the Caribbean Sea.

PNG.name: Papua New Guinea
PNG.geographicScope: Papua New Guinea profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PNG.relationship: Oceania, group of islands including the eastern half of the island of New Guinea between the Coral Sea and the South Pacific Ocean, east of Indonesia. Independent country.
PNG.languages: Tok Pisin, English, Hiri Motu and hundreds of Indigenous languages.
PNG.highlight: Shares island of New Guinea with Indonesia; highlands that trend from east to west break up New Guinea into diverse ecoregions; one of world's largest swamps lies along the southwest coast.

PRY.name: Paraguay
PRY.geographicScope: Paraguay profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PRY.relationship: Central South America, northeast of Argentina, southwest of Brazil. Independent country.
PRY.languages: Guarani and Spanish; Portuguese, German and other Indigenous languages.
PRY.highlight: Landlocked; lies between Argentina, Bolivia, and Brazil; population concentrated in eastern and southern part of country.

CHN.name: People's Republic of China
CHN.geographicScope: Mainland-China profile, excluding separately mapped Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan; disputed boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2 rather than a recognition claim.
CHN.relationship: Independent country in eastern Asia; Hong Kong and Macao are special administrative regions and are mapped separately. Taiwan is self-governed and separately mapped.
CHN.languages: Mandarin Chinese, Cantonese, Wu, Min, Hakka and many other languages, including Tibetan, Uyghur and Mongolian.
CHN.highlight: Western mountains, high plateaus and deserts contrast with eastern plains and river deltas.

PER.name: Peru
PER.geographicScope: Peru profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
