PER.relationship: Western South America, bordering the South Pacific Ocean, between Chile and Ecuador. Independent country.
PER.languages: Spanish, Quechua and Aymara; Ashaninka and other Amazonian languages.
PER.highlight: Peru combines a Pacific coastal plain, the high Andes and lowland Amazonian forest.

PHL.name: Philippines
PHL.geographicScope: Philippines profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PHL.relationship: Southeastern Asia, archipelago between the Philippine Sea and the South China Sea, east of Vietnam. Independent country.
PHL.languages: Tagalog, Bisaya, Hiligaynon, Ilocano, Cebuano, Bikol, Waray and many other languages; Filipino and English are official.
PHL.highlight: For decades, the Philippine archipelago was reported as having 7,107 islands; in 2016, the national mapping authority reported that hundreds of new islands had been discovered and increased the number of islands to 7,641, though not all of the new islands have been verified.

PCN.name: Pitcairn Islands
PCN.geographicScope: Pitcairn Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PCN.relationship: Oceania, islands in the South Pacific Ocean, about midway between Peru and New Zealand. Overseas territory of the UK.
PCN.languages: English and Pitkern, which has English and Tahitian roots.

population.note: Archived population figure; “stable” reflects a rounded 0% growth estimate for 2014, not a claim about current change.

PCN.highlight: Britain's most isolated dependency; only the larger island of Pitcairn is inhabited, but it has no port or natural harbor; supplies must be transported by longboat from larger ships stationed offshore.

POL.name: Poland
POL.geographicScope: Poland profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
POL.relationship: Central Europe, east of Germany. Independent country.
POL.languages: Polish and Silesian, among other languages.
POL.highlight: Most of Poland is a flat plain, while mountains line its southern border.

PRT.name: Portugal
PRT.geographicScope: Portugal profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PRT.relationship: Southwestern Europe, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, west of Spain. Independent country.
PRT.highlight: Azores and Madeira Islands occupy strategic locations along western sea approaches to Strait of Gibraltar; they are two of the four North Atlantic archipelagos that make up Macaronesia; the others are the Canary Islands (Spain) and Cabo Verde.

PRI.name: Puerto Rico
PRI.geographicScope: Puerto Rico profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
PRI.relationship: Caribbean, island between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, east of the Dominican Republic. Unincorporated organized territory of the US with commonwealth status.
PRI.highlight: Puerto Rico has a mountainous interior, a northern coastal plain and sandy beaches along much of its coast.

QAT.name: Qatar
QAT.geographicScope: Qatar profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
QAT.relationship: Middle East, peninsula bordering the Persian Gulf and Saudi Arabia. Independent country.
QAT.languages: Arabic; English is commonly used as a second language.
QAT.highlight: Most of the peninsula is flat desert, with low hills rather than high mountain ranges.

COG.name: Republic of the Congo
COG.geographicScope: Republic of the Congo profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
COG.relationship: Central Africa, bordering the South Atlantic Ocean, between Angola and Gabon. Independent country.
COG.languages: French, Lingala, Kituba (Monokutuba), Kikongo and other languages.
COG.highlight: The landscape includes a coastal plain, central plateau and the low-lying Congo Basin.

ROU.name: Romania
ROU.geographicScope: Romania profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ROU.relationship: Southeastern Europe, bordering the Black Sea, between Bulgaria and Ukraine. Independent country.
ROU.highlight: Controls the most easily traversable land route between the Balkans, Moldova, and Ukraine; the Carpathian Mountains dominate the center of the country, and the Danube River forms much of the southern boundary with Serbia and Bulgaria.

RUS.name: Russia
RUS.geographicScope: Russia national profile; the source estimate is not a census of the exact Natural Earth map polygons, particularly in disputed areas of Ukraine.
RUS.relationship: North Asia bordering the Arctic Ocean, extending from Eastern Europe (the portion west of the Urals) to the North Pacific Ocean. Independent country.
RUS.languages: Russian, Tatar, Chechen and many other languages.
RUS.highlight: The landscape extends from plains west of the Urals across Siberian forest and tundra to mountains in the south and east.

RWA.name: Rwanda
RWA.geographicScope: Rwanda profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
RWA.relationship: Central Africa, east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, north of Burundi. Independent country.
RWA.highlight: Landlocked; most of the country is intensively cultivated and rugged, with the population predominantly rural.

BLM.name: Saint Barthélemy
BLM.geographicScope: Saint Barthélemy overseas collectivity only, not metropolitan France or the other French Caribbean territories.
BLM.relationship: French overseas collectivity in the Caribbean, east of the Virgin Islands.
BLM.highlight: A 1,200-hectare (3,000-acre) marine nature reserve, the Reserve Naturelle, is made up of five zones around the island that form a network to protect the island's coral reefs, seagrass, and endangered marine species.

SHN.name: Saint Helena
SHN.geographicScope: Source covers Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha together. At this map scale only Saint Helena and Ascension are drawn; the territory-wide population is explicitly retained.
SHN.relationship: British overseas territory in the South Atlantic, comprising Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha.

population.note: Archived estimate for Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha together.

SHN.highlight: Saint Helena harbors at least 40 species of plants unknown elsewhere in the world.

KNA.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
KNA.geographicScope: Saint Kitts and Nevis profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
KNA.relationship: Caribbean, islands in the Caribbean Sea, about one-third of the way from Puerto Rico to Trinidad and Tobago. Independent country.
KNA.highlight: Smallest country in the Western Hemisphere in terms of both area and population.

LCA.name: Saint Lucia
LCA.geographicScope: Saint Lucia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LCA.relationship: Caribbean, island between the Caribbean Sea and North Atlantic Ocean, north of Trinidad and Tobago. Independent country.
LCA.highlight: The twin Pitons (Gros Piton and Petit Piton), striking cone-shaped peaks south of Soufrière, are one of the scenic natural highlights of the Caribbean.

MAF.name: Saint Martin
MAF.geographicScope: French Saint Martin, the northern part of the island only; excludes Dutch Sint Maarten and metropolitan France.
MAF.relationship: French overseas collectivity occupying the northern part of the Caribbean island shared with Sint Maarten.
MAF.languages: French, English, Dutch, Caribbean creoles, Spanish and other languages.
MAF.highlight: Saint Martin shares its island with Sint Maarten, with the French collectivity in the north and the Dutch constituent country in the south.

SPM.name: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
SPM.geographicScope: Saint Pierre and Miquelon profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SPM.relationship: Northern North America, islands in the North Atlantic Ocean, south of Newfoundland (Canada). Overseas collectivity of France.
SPM.highlight: Vegetation scanty; the islands are part of the northern Appalachians, along with Newfoundland.

VCT.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
VCT.geographicScope: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
VCT.relationship: Caribbean, islands between the Caribbean Sea and North Atlantic Ocean, north of Trinidad and Tobago. Independent country.
VCT.languages: English, Vincentian Creole English and French-based Creole.
VCT.highlight: The administration of the islands of the Grenadines group is divided between Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and Grenada; Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is composed of 32 islands and cays.

WSM.name: Samoa
WSM.geographicScope: Samoa profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
WSM.relationship: Oceania, group of islands in the South Pacific Ocean, about halfway between Hawaii and New Zealand. Independent country.
WSM.highlight: Occupies an almost central position within Polynesia.

SMR.name: San Marino
SMR.geographicScope: San Marino profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SMR.relationship: Southern Europe, an enclave in central Italy. Independent country.
SMR.highlight: Landlocked; an enclave of (completely surrounded by) Italy; smallest independent state in Europe after the Holy See and Monaco; dominated by the Apennine Mountains.

STP.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
STP.geographicScope: São Tomé and Príncipe profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
STP.relationship: Central Africa, islands in the Gulf of Guinea, just north of the Equator, west of Gabon. Independent country.
STP.languages: Portuguese and Portuguese-based creoles including Forro, Angolar and Lung’ie.
STP.highlight: The second-smallest African country (after the Seychelles); the two main islands form part of a chain of extinct volcanoes, and both are mountainous.

SAU.name: Saudi Arabia
SAU.geographicScope: Saudi Arabia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SAU.relationship: Middle East, bordering the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea, north of Yemen. Independent country.
SAU.highlight: Saudi Arabia is the largest country in the world without a river; extensive coastlines on the Persian Gulf and Red Sea allow for considerable shipping (especially of crude oil) through the Persian Gulf and Suez Canal.

SEN.name: Senegal
SEN.geographicScope: Senegal profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SEN.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Guinea-Bissau and Mauritania. Independent country.
SEN.languages: French, Wolof, Pulaar, Jola, Mandinka, Serer and Soninke.
SEN.highlight: Westernmost country on the African continent; The Gambia is almost an enclave within Senegal.

SRB.name: Serbia
SRB.geographicScope: Serbia profile excluding separately mapped Kosovo; geographic inclusion is not a statement about Kosovo’s recognition.
SRB.relationship: Southeastern Europe, between Macedonia and Hungary. Independent country.
SRB.languages: Serbian; Hungarian, Bosnian, Romani and other minority languages.
SRB.highlight: Fertile northern plains contrast with limestone ranges in the east and older mountains in the southeast.

SYC.name: Seychelles
SYC.geographicScope: Seychelles profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SYC.relationship: Archipelago in the Indian Ocean, northeast of Madagascar. Independent country.
SYC.highlight: The Seychelles include both high islands and low coral atolls; Morne Seychellois rises to 905 metres.

KAS.name: Siachen Glacier
KAS.geographicScope: The separately mapped Siachen Glacier area in disputed Kashmir; not India’s or Pakistan’s national population.
KAS.relationship: High-altitude glacier in the Karakoram, near Indian-, Pakistani- and Chinese-administered territory; India and Pakistan dispute the area.
KAS.languages: No resident-language census is available for the mapped glacier.

population.period: No comparable resident-population series for the glacier.
population.note: NASA describes this remote area as uninhabited. Natural Earth’s undetailed population estimate is not used as a resident census; rotating military presence is not a civilian count.

KAS.highlight: NASA describes a glacier about 75 km long, fed by tributary glaciers whose rock debris forms dark parallel moraines.

SLE.name: Sierra Leone
SLE.geographicScope: Sierra Leone profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SLE.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Guinea and Liberia. Independent country.
SLE.highlight: Rainfall along the coast can reach 495 cm (195 in) a year, making it one of the wettest places along coastal western Africa.

SGP.name: Singapore
SGP.geographicScope: Singapore profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SGP.relationship: Southeastern Asia, islands between Malaysia and Indonesia. Independent country.
SGP.languages: English, Mandarin, Malay and Tamil; Hokkien, Cantonese and other Chinese languages.
SGP.highlight: Focal point for Southeast Asian sea routes; consists of about 60 islands, the largest of which by far is Pulau Ujong; land reclamation has removed many former islands and created a number of new ones.

SXM.name: Sint Maarten
SXM.geographicScope: Dutch Sint Maarten, the southern part of the island only; excludes French Saint Martin and the European Netherlands.
SXM.relationship: Constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands on the southern part of the Caribbean island shared with Saint Martin.
SXM.languages: English and Dutch; Spanish, creoles, Papiamento and French are also spoken.
SXM.highlight: Sint Maarten shares its island with Saint Martin, with the Dutch constituent country in the south and the French collectivity in the north.

SVK.name: Slovakia
SVK.geographicScope: Slovakia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SVK.relationship: Central Europe, south of Poland. Independent country.
SVK.highlight: Landlocked; most of the country is rugged and mountainous; the Tatra Mountains in the north are interspersed with many scenic lakes and valleys.

SVN.name: Slovenia
SVN.geographicScope: Slovenia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SVN.relationship: South Central Europe, Julian Alps between Austria and Croatia. Independent country.
SVN.languages: Slovene; Croatian, Serbian, Bosnian, Hungarian and Italian are also spoken.
SVN.highlight: Despite its small size, this eastern Alpine country controls some of Europe's major transit routes.

SLB.name: Solomon Islands
SLB.geographicScope: Solomon Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SLB.relationship: Oceania, group of islands in the South Pacific Ocean, east of Papua New Guinea. Independent country.
SLB.languages: Solomon Islands Pijin, English and many Indigenous languages.
SLB.highlight: The archipelago combines rugged mountainous islands with low coral atolls.

SOM.name: Somalia
SOM.geographicScope: Somalia’s national statistical profile includes Somaliland, although Somaliland is separately mapped. This count is not an estimate for only the remainder polygon and must not be added to Somaliland’s count.
SOM.relationship: Independent country in the Horn of Africa, east of Ethiopia; the self-administered Somaliland map entity is shown separately, without implying recognition.
SOM.languages: Somali and Arabic; Italian and English are also spoken.

population.note: National estimate includes the separately mapped Somaliland; not a remainder-area count.

SOM.highlight: Somalia occupies the Horn of Africa beside routes linking the Indian Ocean, Gulf of Aden and Red Sea.

SOL.name: Somaliland
SOL.geographicScope: The self-administered Somaliland entity in Natural Earth 5.1.2; its territorial claims and areas of control do not necessarily coincide.
SOL.relationship: Self-administered territory on the Gulf of Aden in the Horn of Africa, claimed by Somalia; shown separately under the map’s de facto-boundary policy.
SOL.languages: Somali and Arabic; English is also used.

population.period: Only one estimate (2014) is supplied for this Natural Earth entity.
population.note: Natural Earth cartographic estimate, not a verified census; the release gives no underlying census methodology or comparable series. Somalia’s national population is not substituted.

SOL.highlight: Northern Somali terrain rises from plateaus toward hills; Somaliland has developed institutions separately from Somalia’s central government.

ZAF.name: South Africa
ZAF.geographicScope: South Africa profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ZAF.relationship: Southern Africa, at the southern tip of the continent of Africa. Independent country.
ZAF.languages: Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans, Sepedi, Setswana, English, Sesotho and other languages, including South African Sign Language.
ZAF.highlight: South Africa completely surrounds Lesotho and almost completely surrounds Eswatini.

SGS.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
SGS.geographicScope: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands only; the source reports no permanent inhabitants, not Argentina’s or the United Kingdom’s population.
SGS.relationship: UK-administered overseas territory in the South Atlantic, east of southern South America; also claimed by Argentina.
SGS.languages: No permanent resident language community; the source does not enumerate station personnel’s languages.

population.period: No dated resident-population series in the archived source.
population.note: The archived source reports no permanent inhabitants; temporary personnel are not a resident population.

SGS.highlight: The north coast of South Georgia has several large bays, which provide good anchorage.

KOR.name: South Korea
KOR.geographicScope: South Korea profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
KOR.relationship: Eastern Asia, southern half of the Korean Peninsula bordering the Sea of Japan and the Yellow Sea. Independent country.
KOR.highlight: Strategic location on Korea Strait; about 3,000 mostly small and uninhabited islands lie off the western and southern coasts.

SDS.name: South Sudan
SDS.geographicScope: South Sudan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SDS.relationship: East-Central Africa; south of Sudan, north of Uganda and Kenya, west of Ethiopia. Independent country.
SDS.languages: English, Arabic varieties including Juba Arabic, Dinka, Nuer, Bari, Zande and Shilluk.

population.note: Archived estimate; conflict and displacement create substantial uncertainty.

SDS.highlight: Landlocked; The Sudd is a vast swamp in the north central region of South Sudan, formed by the White Nile; its size is variable but can reach some 15% of the country's total area during the rainy season; it is one of the world's largest wetlands.

ESP.name: Spain
ESP.geographicScope: Spain profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ESP.relationship: Southwestern Europe, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, North Atlantic Ocean, Bay of Biscay, and Pyrenees Mountains; southwest of France. Independent country.
ESP.languages: Spanish, Catalan/Valencian, Galician, Basque and Aranese.
ESP.highlight: An interior plateau and the Pyrenees contrast with the volcanic Canary Islands, where Teide reaches 3,718 metres.

LKA.name: Sri Lanka
LKA.geographicScope: Sri Lanka profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
LKA.relationship: Southern Asia, island in the Indian Ocean, south of India. Independent country.
LKA.languages: Sinhala and Tamil; English is also spoken.
LKA.highlight: Low coastal plains surround a mountainous south-central interior; Pidurutalagala reaches 2,524 metres.

SDN.name: Sudan
SDN.geographicScope: Sudan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SDN.relationship: North-eastern Africa, bordering the Red Sea, between Egypt and Eritrea. Independent country.
SDN.languages: Arabic, English, Nubian languages, Beja and Fur.

population.note: Archived estimate; conflict and displacement create substantial uncertainty.

SDN.highlight: The Nile is Sudan's primary water source; its major tributaries, the White Nile and the Blue Nile, meet at Khartoum to form the River Nile, which flows northward through Egypt to the Mediterranean Sea.

SUR.name: Suriname
SUR.geographicScope: Suriname profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SUR.relationship: Northern South America, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between French Guiana and Guyana. Independent country.
SUR.languages: Dutch, Sranan Tongo, English, Caribbean Hindustani and Javanese.
SUR.highlight: Smallest independent country on the South American continent; mostly tropical rainforest; great diversity of flora and fauna; relatively small population, mostly along the coast.

SWE.name: Sweden
SWE.geographicScope: Sweden profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SWE.relationship: Northern Europe, bordering the Baltic Sea, Gulf of Bothnia, Kattegat, and Skagerrak, between Finland and Norway. Independent country.
SWE.languages: Swedish; Finnish, Sami, Meänkieli, Romani and Yiddish are minority languages.
SWE.highlight: Strategic location along Danish Straits linking Baltic and North Seas; Sweden has almost 100,000 lakes, the largest of which, Vanern, is the third-largest in Europe.

CHE.name: Switzerland
CHE.geographicScope: Switzerland profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
CHE.relationship: Central Europe, east of France, north of Italy. Independent country.
CHE.languages: German/Swiss German, French, Italian and Romansh; other community languages are also spoken.
CHE.highlight: Landlocked; crossroads of northern and southern Europe; along with southeastern France, northern Italy, and southwestern Austria, has the highest elevations in the Alps.

SYR.name: Syria
SYR.geographicScope: Syria profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
SYR.relationship: Middle East, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, between Lebanon and Turkey. Independent country.
SYR.languages: Arabic, Kurdish, Armenian, Aramaic, Circassian, French and English.

population.note: Archived estimate; conflict and displacement create substantial uncertainty.

SYR.highlight: Damascus lies at an oasis supplied by the Barada River and has a long history of continuous habitation.

TWN.name: Taiwan
TWN.geographicScope: Taiwan source profile, separate from the People’s Republic of China; map inclusion and country naming do not decide sovereignty.
TWN.relationship: Self-governed island polity east of mainland China, across the Taiwan Strait; claimed by the People’s Republic of China, with international status disputed.
TWN.languages: Mandarin, Taiwanese Hokkien (Min Nan), Hakka and Indigenous languages.
TWN.highlight: Rugged mountains cover much of eastern Taiwan, while the west has flatter plains; Yu Shan reaches 3,952 metres.

TJK.name: Tajikistan
TJK.geographicScope: Tajikistan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TJK.relationship: Central Asia, west of China, south of Kyrgyzstan. Independent country.
TJK.highlight: The Pamir mountain region contains Qullai Ismoili Somoni, the highest peak of the former Soviet Union.

TZA.name: Tanzania
TZA.geographicScope: Tanzania profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TZA.relationship: Eastern Africa, bordering the Indian Ocean, between Kenya and Mozambique. Independent country.
TZA.languages: Swahili and English; Arabic and many local languages are also spoken.
TZA.highlight: Kilimanjaro is Africa’s highest mountain; Tanzania also shares Lake Victoria with Kenya and Uganda.

THA.name: Thailand
THA.geographicScope: Thailand profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
THA.relationship: Southeastern Asia, bordering the Andaman Sea and the Gulf of Thailand, southeast of Burma. Independent country.
THA.languages: Thai; Malay, Burmese and other languages; English is also used.
THA.highlight: A central plain contrasts with the Khorat Plateau in the east and mountain ranges elsewhere.

BHS.name: The Bahamas
BHS.geographicScope: The Bahamas profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
BHS.relationship: Chain of islands in the North Atlantic Ocean, southeast of Florida, northeast of Cuba; note - although The Bahamas does not border the Caribbean Sea, geopolitically it is often designated as a Caribbean nation. Independent country.
BHS.languages: English; Haitian Creole is spoken in Haitian communities.
BHS.highlight: Strategic location adjacent to US and Cuba; extensive island chain of which 30 are inhabited.

GMB.name: The Gambia
GMB.geographicScope: The Gambia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
GMB.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean and Senegal. Independent country.
GMB.languages: English, Mandinka, Wolof, Fula and other languages.
GMB.highlight: Almost an enclave of Senegal; smallest country on the African mainland.

TGO.name: Togo
TGO.geographicScope: Togo profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TGO.relationship: Western Africa, bordering the Bight of Benin, between Benin and Ghana. Independent country.
TGO.languages: French, Ewe, Mina, Kabye and Dagomba.
TGO.highlight: Stretches through six distinct geographic regions; climate varies from tropical to savanna.

TON.name: Tonga
TON.geographicScope: Tonga profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TON.relationship: Oceania, archipelago in the South Pacific Ocean, about two-thirds of the way from Hawaii to New Zealand. Independent country.
TON.highlight: The western islands (making up the Tongan Volcanic Arch) are all of volcanic origin; the eastern islands are nonvolcanic and are composed of coral limestone and sand.

TTO.name: Trinidad and Tobago
TTO.geographicScope: Trinidad and Tobago profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TTO.relationship: Caribbean, islands between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, northeast of Venezuela. Independent country.
TTO.languages: English, Trinidadian and Tobagonian creoles, Caribbean Hindustani, Spanish and other languages.
TTO.highlight: Pitch Lake, on Trinidad's southwestern coast, is the world's largest natural reservoir of asphalt.

TUN.name: Tunisia
TUN.geographicScope: Tunisia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TUN.relationship: Northern Africa, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, between Algeria and Libya. Independent country.
TUN.highlight: Terrain: mountains in north; hot, dry central plain; semiarid south merges into the Sahara; highest point: Jebel ech Chambi 1,544 m.

TUR.name: Turkey
TUR.geographicScope: Turkey profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TUR.relationship: Independent country spanning southeastern Europe and western Asia, controlling the Bosporus and Dardanelles between the Black and Aegean seas.
TUR.languages: Turkish, Kurdish and other minority languages.
TUR.highlight: Strategic location controlling the Turkish Straits (Bosporus, Sea of Marmara, Dardanelles) that link the Black and Aegean Seas.

CYN.name: Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus
CYN.geographicScope: Turkish Cypriot-administered northern Cyprus only, not the whole island. The name follows the map and does not imply recognition.
CYN.relationship: Self-administered northern part of Cyprus, south of Turkey in the eastern Mediterranean; its declared state is recognized only by Turkey and claimed by the Republic of Cyprus.
CYN.languages: Turkish; this entry describes the Turkish Cypriot-administered north, not the whole island.

population.note: The Turkish Cypriot Statistical Institute reports 256,644 in 2006 and 286,257 in 2011. Historical census comparison, not a current population estimate.

CYN.highlight: Northern Cyprus occupies part of the Mediterranean’s third-largest island, separated from the south by a UN-patrolled buffer zone.

TKM.name: Turkmenistan
TKM.geographicScope: Turkmenistan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TKM.relationship: Central Asia, bordering the Caspian Sea, between Iran and Kazakhstan. Independent country.
TKM.highlight: Landlocked; the western and central low-lying desolate portions of the country make up the great Garagum (Kara-Kum) desert, which occupies over 80% of the country; eastern part is plateau.

TCA.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
TCA.geographicScope: Turks and Caicos Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TCA.relationship: British overseas territory of two island groups southeast of The Bahamas and north of Haiti.
TCA.highlight: Low limestone islands support extensive marshes and mangrove swamps.

TUV.name: Tuvalu
TUV.geographicScope: Tuvalu profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
TUV.relationship: Oceania, island group consisting of nine coral atolls in the South Pacific Ocean, about half way from Hawaii to Australia. Independent country.
TUV.languages: Tuvaluan and English; Samoan and Kiribati are also spoken.
TUV.highlight: One of the smallest and most remote countries on earth; six of the nine coral atolls -- Nanumea, Nui, Vaitupu, Nukufetau, Funafuti, and Nukulaelae -- have lagoons open to the ocean; Nanumaya and Niutao have landlocked lagoons; Niulakita does not have a lagoon.

UGA.name: Uganda
UGA.geographicScope: Uganda profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
UGA.relationship: East-Central Africa, west of Kenya, east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Independent country.
UGA.languages: English, Swahili, Luganda and many other Niger-Congo and Nilo-Saharan languages.
UGA.highlight: Landlocked; fertile, well-watered country with many lakes and rivers; Lake Victoria, the world's largest tropical lake and second-largest freshwater lake, is shared among three countries: Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.

UKR.name: Ukraine
UKR.geographicScope: Ukraine national statistical profile. War and displacement limit comparison with the map’s fixed de facto boundaries; this is not a population count of territory controlled on retrieval day.
UKR.relationship: Eastern Europe, bordering the Black Sea, between Poland, Belarus, Romania, and Moldova in the west and Russia in the east. Independent country.
UKR.languages: Ukrainian and Russian; Crimean Tatar, Romanian and Hungarian minorities.

population.note: Archived estimate; conflict and displacement create substantial uncertainty.

UKR.highlight: Fertile steppe plains and plateaus dominate much of Ukraine; the Carpathians rise in the west.

ARE.name: United Arab Emirates
ARE.geographicScope: United Arab Emirates profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ARE.relationship: Middle East, bordering the Gulf of Oman and the Persian Gulf, between Oman and Saudi Arabia. Independent country.
ARE.languages: Arabic, English, Hindi, Malayalam, Urdu, Pashto, Tagalog and Persian.
ARE.highlight: The coastal plain merges into rolling desert dunes, while mountains rise in the east.

GBR.name: United Kingdom
GBR.geographicScope: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland; Crown dependencies and overseas territories have separate profiles and populations.
GBR.relationship: Western Europe, islands - including the northern one-sixth of the island of Ireland - between the North Atlantic Ocean and the North Sea; northwest of France. Independent country.
GBR.languages: English; Welsh, Scots, Scottish Gaelic, Irish and Cornish are also used.
GBR.highlight: Lies near vital North Atlantic sea lanes; only 35 km (22 mi) from France and linked by tunnel under the English Channel (the Channel Tunnel or Chunnel); because of heavily indented coastline, no location is more than 125 km (78 mi) from tidal waters.

USA.name: United States of America
USA.geographicScope: United States national profile; Puerto Rico, Guam, the US Virgin Islands, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands are separately mapped territories.
USA.relationship: North America, bordering both the North Atlantic Ocean and the North Pacific Ocean, between Canada and Mexico. Independent country.
USA.languages: English and Spanish; Chinese languages and many other languages.
USA.highlight: The landscape spans central plains, western mountains, Alaska’s rugged ranges and Hawaii’s volcanic islands.

VIR.name: United States Virgin Islands
VIR.geographicScope: United States Virgin Islands profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
VIR.relationship: US territory in the Caribbean, east of Puerto Rico, sharing the Virgin Islands archipelago with the British Virgin Islands.
VIR.languages: English, Spanish and Spanish- and French-based creoles.
VIR.highlight: Important location along the Anegada Passage, a key shipping lane for the Panama Canal; Saint Thomas has one of the best natural deepwater harbors in the Caribbean.

URY.name: Uruguay
URY.geographicScope: Uruguay profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
URY.relationship: Southern South America, bordering the South Atlantic Ocean, between Argentina and Brazil. Independent country.
URY.highlight: Second-smallest South American country (after Suriname); most of the low-lying landscape (three-quarters of the country) is grassland, ideal for cattle and sheep.

UZB.name: Uzbekistan
UZB.geographicScope: Uzbekistan profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
UZB.relationship: Central Asia, north of Turkmenistan, south of Kazakhstan. Independent country.
UZB.highlight: Along with Liechtenstein, one of the only two doubly landlocked countries in the world.

VUT.name: Vanuatu
VUT.geographicScope: Vanuatu profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
VUT.relationship: Oceania, group of islands in the South Pacific Ocean, about three-quarters of the way from Hawaii to Australia. Independent country.
VUT.languages: Bislama, English, French and more than a hundred Indigenous languages.
VUT.highlight: A Y-shaped chain of four main islands and 80 smaller islands; several of the islands have active volcanoes, including several underwater volcanoes.

VAT.name: Vatican City
VAT.geographicScope: Vatican City profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
VAT.relationship: Southern Europe, an enclave of Rome (Italy). Independent country.
VAT.languages: Italian, Latin, French and many other languages.

population.note: Archived population figure; “stable” reflects a rounded 0% growth estimate for 2014, not a claim about current change.

VAT.highlight: Landlocked; an enclave in Rome, Italy; world's smallest state.

VEN.name: Venezuela
VEN.geographicScope: Venezuela profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
VEN.relationship: Northern South America, bordering the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, between Colombia and Guyana. Independent country.
VEN.highlight: Venezuela combines the Andes and Maracaibo lowlands in the northwest, central llanos plains and the Guiana Highlands in the southeast.

VNM.name: Vietnam
VNM.geographicScope: Vietnam profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
VNM.relationship: Southeastern Asia, bordering the Gulf of Thailand, Gulf of Tonkin, and South China Sea, as well as China, Laos, and Cambodia. Independent country.
VNM.languages: Vietnamese; English, Chinese, Khmer and numerous mountain-community languages are also spoken.
VNM.highlight: Extending 1,650 km (1,025 mi) north to south, the country is only 50 km (31 mi) across at its narrowest point.

WLF.name: Wallis and Futuna
WLF.geographicScope: Wallis and Futuna profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
WLF.relationship: Oceania, islands in the South Pacific Ocean, about two-thirds of the way from Hawaii to New Zealand. Overseas collectivity of France.
WLF.highlight: Both island groups have fringing reefs; Wallis contains several prominent crater lakes.

SAH.name: Western Sahara
SAH.geographicScope: The separately mapped Western Sahara territory, not Morocco’s population. Uses the archived 2020 Western Sahara profile, predating its removal from later Factbook editions.
SAH.relationship: Disputed territory on Africa’s Atlantic coast between Morocco and Mauritania; claimed by Morocco and the Sahrawi independence movement. Map inclusion does not settle sovereignty.
SAH.languages: Hassaniya Arabic, other Arabic varieties, Amazigh languages, Spanish and French.
SAH.highlight: The waters off the coast are particularly rich fishing areas.

YEM.name: Yemen
YEM.geographicScope: Yemen profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
YEM.relationship: Middle East, bordering the Arabian Sea, Gulf of Aden, and Red Sea, between Oman and Saudi Arabia. Independent country.

population.note: Archived estimate; conflict and displacement create substantial uncertainty.

YEM.highlight: Strategic location on Bab el Mandeb, the strait linking the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden and one of world's most active shipping lanes.

ZMB.name: Zambia
ZMB.geographicScope: Zambia profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ZMB.relationship: Southern Africa, east of Angola, south of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Independent country.
ZMB.languages: Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga, Lozi, Chewa, English and many other languages.
ZMB.highlight: Landlocked; the Zambezi forms a natural river boundary with Zimbabwe; Lake Kariba on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border forms the world's largest reservoir by volume (180 cu km; 43 cu mi).

ZWE.name: Zimbabwe
ZWE.geographicScope: Zimbabwe profile; map boundaries follow Natural Earth 5.1.2, not a live boundary service.
ZWE.relationship: Southern Africa, between South Africa and Zambia. Independent country.
ZWE.languages: Shona, Ndebele, English and other languages including Chewa, Kalanga, Tonga, Venda and sign language.
ZWE.highlight: Terrain: mostly high plateau with higher central plateau (high veld); mountains in east; highest point: Inyangani 2,592 m.
